items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: At first, he turned me over to his star pupil, who was very advanced, and his name was Rudy Powell, and then I studied with him for a little while

ctx.x: Which he did help me. It wasn't too much easier, because nothing like that is easy until you really study it, you know, to a certain degree. After which I studied with him for a while -- and when I say a while, it was quite a short while, because he didn't read music, but he could show me things about the instrument, you know? * see p 63, not whom for spelling

And then I went to a teacher named Michael -- what was his first name? Eugene. Yes. And I studied with him for a while; he also had 2 sons who were fine musicians -- Otto and Gene Jr. After studying with him a while, he turned me over -- well, at the beginning, he turned me over to who was his star pupil, Rudy Powell, who was a very fine musician. Rudy had also played violin.

Then after I studied with Michael a while -- I don't remember how long -- I went to a teacher named Arthur Reeves, with whom I studied for, oh, maybe a year or more -- and he was a very, very fine saxophone player. I tried to develop the sound that he was getting because the sound that he got was great.

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: considering I was a beginner, he had his assistant teach me and spend as much time with me as Professor Michaels himself did. His assistant was Rudy Powell

ctx.x: Can you remember any of the other people that you worked with early on?

Actually, the teacher that he recommended first was a professor, Eugene Michaels, who had been in the army or whatever service, some military service, and, considering I was a beginner, he had his assistant teach me and spend as much time with me as Professor Michaels himself did. His assistant was Rudy Powell, who came to be known later as a very great, fine lead player with some of the orchestras around that time.
Let’s see. Did we mention . . . we didn’t mention Arthur Reeves at all?
